title: Sample 15-8: Poem with Line Numbers and Rhyme Scheme

illustrates.quote: Poetry with Line-Numbered Rhyme Scheme. Observe the following guidelines, in addition to the points outlined in Formats, §15.7.2: a. Use poetry format. (See Formats, §13, Poetry and Song Lyrics.) b. Follow print for line numbers. Do not add numbers that do not occur in print. c. Place line numbers, preceded by the numeric indicator, at the right margin. d. Position the letters of the rhyme scheme so that they end one cell before the longest line number on the braille page.

blocks.text: I wonder do you feel to-day
As I have felt since, hand in hand,
We sat down on the grass, to stray
In spirit better through the land,
This morn of Rome and May?
For me, I touched a thought, I know,
(Like turns of thread the spiders throw
Mocking across our path) for rhymes
To catch at and let go.

resolution: Braille unchanged (A and B agree, already verified verbatim). Print side: both runs wrongly included the sample's own citation title as a print.blocks heading — removed, since the given braille has no row for it (matching every other file in this section); wording/letters/numbers otherwise already agreed; levels re-measured directly from the braille. Modeled by buildModel15 as a genuine poem (kind:'verse') whose 'letter' field is folded into the line's own text as a literal prefix (matching parsePoem's real numPrefix behaviour, F-182) on EVERY line; the 'number' field on lines 5/10 is deliberately NOT built — per standards-map.md's own row for 15.7.3d and standards-findings.md F-182, parse.mjs's findLinenum returns only the FIRST <linenum> child of a poem line, so when a line carries both a letter and a number the second marker (the number) is silently dropped, not merely misplaced. This file's mismatch cause is F-182 twice over: left-margin placement of the letter, AND total loss of the line number on lines 5/10.
